transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been feeling… not quite real, I guess. Or like things around me aren’t real. The thing that scares me most is when I’m walking across campus — I work there as a teaching assistant — and it’s like I’m seeing everything through glass. I can see the buildings, the students moving around, people talking, all the normal campus things, but it feels distant, like there’s a pane between me and the world.

And sometimes it’s not just the outside stuff. It feels like I’m not fully in my own body, like I’m watching myself walk rather than actually being the one walking. I know that sounds strange. I know where I am, I know it’s campus, I know the students and buildings are real, but in the moment they feel slightly unreal, and that really frightens me. I don’t feel like myself when it happens.
Do these feelings of unreality happen more often during times of stress, or do they seem to come out of the blue?

It’s… I want to say it happens more when I’m stressed, but honestly the part that frightens me is that it can feel like it just arrives while I’m doing something ordinary, like walking across campus. I’ll be going between buildings or passing students, and suddenly everything looks normal but feels wrong — like I’m seeing it through glass, or like there’s this thin barrier between me and everything around me.

And then I start feeling like I’m not quite inside myself, if that makes sense. Like I’m watching myself walk instead of just walking. The buildings are there, the students are there, I know they’re real, but they feel slightly unreal in that moment. So I don’t know if it’s always stress exactly. Being on campus can be stressful, but sometimes it feels like it comes out of nowhere, and that makes it worse because I don’t feel like I can predict it.
Can you think of any specific situations, thoughts, or feelings that tend to come up just before these experiences start?

I’ve been trying to figure that out, because it feels like there should be some clear warning sign, but I’m not always sure there is. The situation I can identify most is walking across campus. That seems to be when I notice it most strongly — like I’ll be moving between buildings, seeing students around me, hearing people talking, and then suddenly it’s as if everything is still there but… separated from me somehow.

It’s not that I think the buildings or students aren’t real. I know they are. But right before or as it starts, I get this strange feeling like I’m behind glass, watching it all from slightly far away. And then I become very aware of myself walking, almost too aware, like I’m observing my body doing it instead of just being in it naturally. That’s the part that scares me the most.

I don’t know if there’s always a thought right before it. Sometimes I’m just going about my day, and then the campus around me starts to feel unreal, and I feel not fully in my own body. Then I start thinking, “Oh no, it’s happening again,” and I get frightened by how wrong everything feels.
Do you ever experience moments where you feel detached from yourself — like you're not connected to your own thoughts, feelings, or body — even when the world around you seems completely real?

Yes… yes, that’s actually a big part of it. Sometimes the world around me looks completely normal — like I can see the campus, the buildings, the students walking past, everything is in the right place — but I feel like I’m not quite connected to myself.

It’s hard to explain without sounding strange, but it’s like I’m there and not there at the same time. I’ll be walking, and I know my body is moving, I know I’m the one walking, but it feels almost like I’m observing it from a little distance instead of just being inside myself naturally. Like I’m watching myself do the motions.

And then with the campus, it’s almost mixed together — I feel detached from myself, and the buildings and students around me feel slightly unreal too, like I’m seeing everything through glass. I know they’re real, I’m not confused about that, but emotionally or physically it feels distant. That’s the part that really scares me, because I’ll be doing something ordinary and suddenly I don’t feel fully in my own body.
Have you ever experienced these feelings of detachment or unreality without any other changes in your memory, identity, or sense of who you are?

I think… yes, mostly it happens without me feeling like I’ve become someone else or anything like that. I still know who I am. I know I’m me, I know where I am, I know I’m walking across campus and that those are the buildings and students around me.

It’s more that everything suddenly feels distant or unreal, like I’m watching it through glass. And at the same time I don’t feel fully in my own body, like I’m observing myself walking instead of just walking normally. That’s what scares me most — not that I forget who I am, but that I feel separated from myself and from everything around me, even though I know it’s all real.
Have these episodes ever occurred when you were not in a stressful situation or feeling anxious, or do they always seem to happen during times of heightened anxiety?

It doesn’t always feel like I’m already anxious before it starts. That’s part of what makes it so unsettling. Sometimes I’ll just be walking across campus, doing something completely ordinary, and then suddenly it’s like everything shifts.

I’ll see the buildings and the students around me, and I know they’re real, but it feels like I’m watching it all through glass. And then I become aware that I don’t feel fully in my own body, like I’m somehow observing myself walking instead of just… walking. Once I notice that, then I definitely get scared and anxious, because it feels so wrong.

So I guess anxiety comes in very quickly, but I’m not sure it’s always there first. Sometimes the strange detached feeling seems to happen first, and then I panic because the campus and the people around me feel slightly unreal, and I feel separated from myself.
Have you ever experienced these feelings of detachment or unreality without any other changes, like forgetting parts of your life, feeling like you have different identities, or losing time?

Yes… I mean, as far as I can tell, I don’t lose track of who I am or anything like that. I don’t suddenly think I’m someone else, and I don’t feel like there are different versions of me taking over. It’s not like that.

What scares me most is more this strange distance from myself and from everything around me. Like when I’m walking across campus, I can see the buildings, the students, the sidewalks — everything is there, everything looks normal in a way — but it feels like I’m watching it all through glass. Like there’s something between me and the world.

And at the same time, I don’t feel fully in my own body. I know I’m the one walking, I know those are my legs moving, but it feels almost like I’m watching myself walk instead of just being in it. The buildings and people around me feel slightly unreal, even though I know they’re real. That’s the part that really frightens me. It’s not so much forgetting parts of my life or losing time — it’s that I feel present but not fully connected, if that makes sense.
Have you ever experienced these feelings of being detached from yourself or the world around you as a persistent or ongoing experience, rather than just in brief episodes?

I don’t think it’s there every single minute, no… but it’s more than just one quick flash and then it’s gone, if that makes sense. It can sort of hang around for a while once it starts, especially when I’m walking across campus.

That’s the thing that scares me most — I’ll be going past the buildings and students, and everything is technically normal, but it feels like I’m watching it all through glass. Like the world is there, but I’m not quite in it. And then I start feeling like I’m not fully inside my own body either, like I’m observing myself moving through campus instead of just being myself walking.

So I wouldn’t say it’s constant all day, but when it happens it doesn’t feel like just a second-long thing. It can feel ongoing in that moment, like I’m stuck in this strange separated feeling where the buildings and people around me seem slightly unreal, even though I know they’re real. That’s what makes it so frightening.
Have you experienced these feelings of being detached from yourself or the world around you almost every day for at least a month?

It’s been very frequent, yes… I’m a little unsure how to measure “almost every day,” because some days it’s stronger than others, and there are moments when I’m distracted enough that I don’t notice it. But it does feel like this has been happening again and again over weeks, not just one isolated episode.

The clearest example is when I’m walking across campus. I’ll be going between buildings or passing students, and suddenly everything feels distant, like I’m seeing it through glass. I know where I am, I know those are real people and real buildings, but it doesn’t feel fully real in the moment. And then I get this awful feeling like I’m not completely inside my own body, like I’m watching myself walk instead of just walking normally.

That’s the part that scares me most. It’s not dramatic from the outside, I don’t think anyone would look at me and know anything is wrong, but internally it feels so strange and unsettling. So… yes, it has felt like something that keeps coming back very often, close to daily, for at least that long.
Have these feelings of detachment from yourself or the world ever lasted for hours, days, or even longer without fully going away?

Yes… sometimes it feels like it lasts for hours, or at least it doesn’t fully lift quickly. It’s hard to describe because it can fade in and out, but when it starts, especially when I’m walking across campus, it can sort of stay with me.

I’ll be moving between buildings, passing students, hearing people talking, seeing everything around me, and it all looks normal — but it feels like I’m behind glass somehow. Like I’m there, but not completely connected to what I’m seeing. And then I get this feeling that I’m not fully in my own body, almost like I’m watching myself walk rather than just being the person walking.

It doesn’t always stay at the same intensity the whole time, but it can linger. Even if I try to focus on something else, there’s this unreal quality to the buildings and people around me, like they’re slightly distant or not fully real, even though I know they are. That’s the part that frightens me, because I keep waiting for it to just snap back to normal, and sometimes it doesn’t right away.

Have you ever experienced these feelings of being detached from yourself or the world around you without any other unusual experiences, like feeling like you're a different person, forgetting parts of your life, or finding yourself in places without knowing how you got there?

I think so, yes… at least, the main thing I’m experiencing is that detached feeling. It isn’t like I suddenly believe I’m literally someone else or anything like that. What scares me most is more this strange separation from myself and from everything around me.

Like I keep saying, it happens most noticeably when I’m walking across campus. I’ll see the buildings and the students and the paths and everything is familiar, but it feels like I’m watching it through glass. It’s very unsettling because I know where I am, and I know those things are real, but they feel slightly unreal or distant. And at the same time, I don’t feel fully inside my own body. It’s almost like I’m observing myself walking instead of just being naturally present in it.

So… yes, I’d say the detachment is the thing. The world feels kind of unreal, and I feel not quite connected to myself, but that’s different from feeling like I’m a completely different person. It’s more like I’m still me, but I’m separated from myself and from the campus around me, if that makes sense.

This supports the inclusion of F48.1 (Depersonalization disorder) as a primary candidate, while still maintaining the dissociative disorder codes (F44.4, F44.8, F44.9) as possibilities.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced persistent or recurrent depersonalization or derealization without other dissociative symptoms, which would support a diagnosis of Depersonalization/Derealization Disorder (F48.1).
doctor.question: Have you ever experienced these feelings of being detached from yourself or the world around you without any other unusual experiences, like feeling like you're a different person, forgetting parts of your life, or finding yourself in places without knowing how you got there?

target_item.name: Depersonalization_Derealization
target_item.manifestation: What scares me most is that when I walk across campus, it feels like I’m watching everything through glass, like I’m not fully in my own body and the buildings and students around me are slightly unreal.
target_item.reason: The question is directly about feelings of detachment from self or surroundings, while distinguishing them from other unusual dissociative experiences.

patient.answer:
I think so, yes… at least, the main thing I’m experiencing is that detached feeling. It isn’t like I suddenly believe I’m literally someone else or anything like that. What scares me most is more this strange separation from myself and from everything around me.

Like I keep saying, it happens most noticeably when I’m walking across campus. I’ll see the buildings and the students and the paths and everything is familiar, but it feels like I’m watching it through glass. It’s very unsettling because I know where I am, and I know those things are real, but they feel slightly unreal or distant. And at the same time, I don’t feel fully inside my own body. It’s almost like I’m observing myself walking instead of just being naturally present in it.

So… yes, I’d say the detachment is the thing. The world feels kind of unreal, and I feel not quite connected to myself, but that’s different from feeling like I’m a completely different person. It’s more like I’m still me, but I’m separated from myself and from the campus around me, if that makes sense.

inference.note: The patient's symptoms of persistent or recurrent detachment from self and the environment, without loss of reality testing, identity disturbance, or other dissociative symptoms, are most consistent with depersonalization-derealization disorder (F48.1). Other candidates (F44.4, F44.8, F44.9) have been ruled out due to the chronic and non-trauma-related nature of the symptoms, and the absence of other dissociative or conversion phenomena.
